Based on my analysis, I'll summarize the findings before answering.

**What the data shows for Zone_F3_Z01 (Core_mid):**
- Zone air temperature: H1 2018 mean ≈ 23.1 °C (range 20.3–25.5) → H2 mean ≈ 25.1 °C (range 24.0–27.1), i.e. a ~2 °C upward shift, larger than sibling zones (which rose ~0.4–0.7 °C). So it is a locally-anomalous rise.
- Cooling setpoint: unchanged (≈25.2 °C both halves). Heating setpoint: unchanged (≈18.6 °C both halves).
- VAV damper position setpoint: increased (mean 0.19 → 0.44, max 0.35 → 0.82) — the controller is responding to the higher reading.

**Why the two candidate causes cannot be separated with these streams:**
Under a genuine local load change the controller serves extra heat gain by opening the cooling damper — same signature as a high-biased zone temperature sensor that makes the controller over-cool. Both hypotheses predict exactly the observed pattern (temperature rises, setpoints hold, damper opens more). There is no flatline or step-fault, so a sensor fault is still possible (bias/drift), and no second temperature measurement or actual delivered-cooling measurement exists to confirm the temperature is real vs. spurious.

The available streams (zone air temperature sensor, cooling/heating setpoints, damper position setpoint for F3_Z01) therefore cannot distinguish a real local load change from a faulty sensor reading.
